newsitem.title: UK: Fresh wind may blow BT director ashore.
newsitem.headline: Fresh wind may blow BT director ashore.

text.p: British Telecom is hoping that a fresh wind will blow ashore Alan Rudge, the first BT director to have joined the board of merger partner MCI, in time for what could be a stormy shareholder meeting on Wednesday.
At the annual meeting the Scottish capital of Edinburgh, BT is likely to face a grilling from shareholders concerned at last week's surprise profit warning from MCI Communications Corp.

Rudge, who joined MCI in 1993 when BT bought its first 20 percent MCI stake, is a keen sailor but was stranded offshore as his yacht -- which ironically bears the name of the proposed BT and MCI merged group Concert -- lay becalmed "going nowhere fast", BT said.

Rudge is taking part in the Global Challenge, the BT-sponsored round-the-world yacht-race. But calm weather on the last leg of the race from Boston in the United States to Southampton in southern England had left the fleet in the doldrums.

Rudge was keen to attend BT's annual meeting, which will be his last before he retires this summer. But the company was denied permission to airlift him ashore. Under race rules, this would disqualify Concert unless the airlifted crew member is either injured or sick.
But other plans of sophisticated audio-visual link-ups between the yacht and Edinburgh may now not be needed because the wind has started blowing again, BT said on Tuesday.
"Suddenly the wind picked up and they have made up a lot of time," a BT spokeswoman said. "They are currently heading eastwards and are due to make land early tomorrow."
"It will then be a case of getting him to Edinburgh. We'll get him there, I hope -- but this presumes that the winds keep blowing," she added.

BT's plan to buy the 80 percent of MCI it does not already own in a $24 billion deal which hit its first major set-back on Friday after MCI said it expected up to an additional $1.5 billion of unforeseen losses in the next two years.
